title: Payment Voucher
context: Finance › Payment Flow (Purchase Bill to Vendor Payment) › Payment Voucher

cards.title: Where the Payment Voucher sits in the payment settlement workflow
cards.body:
The Payment Voucher is step seven and the concluding event of the supplier payment flow.
It immediately follows the Payment Advice where payments are authorized for release by treasury.
Accounts officers use this screen to record the physical disbursement of corporate funds.
It executes the actual payment out of company cash boxes or corporate bank accounts.
The voucher settles outstanding vendor liabilities established by earlier purchase bills.
Completing the voucher updates bank balances, vendor accounts, and General Ledger books.
Cheque details, electronic transfer numbers, and payment modes are recorded here.
Authorizing the voucher clears matched purchase bill balances and prevents duplicate payments.
Financial audit trails trace payments directly back through advice, plan, and purchase bill.
This document provides definitive accounting proof that a commercial liability has been paid.
Bank reconciliation features link to this voucher to reconcile cleared payments against statements.
Authorized vouchers become permanent accounting records that cannot be modified retroactively.
Cashiers confirm cheque signatures or electronic transfer authorizations before funds leave accounts.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.

cards.title: Mandatory voucher headers, bank account rules, and date checks
cards.body:
Creating a payment voucher requires critical accounting headers and account selections in the system.
The user must select a valid voucher type, transaction currency, and active finance book.
The document date cannot precede the opening date defined for the selected finance book.
If the finance book is closed for the document date, saving is immediately prohibited.
Every voucher must link to at least one valid company cash or bank ledger account.
Selecting duplicate accounts sharing the same bank or cash type is stopped by the system.
Cheque dates and transfer dates cannot precede the document date of the payment voucher.
Cheque numbers, demand draft numbers, or transaction reference codes are compulsory.
The payee name and designated bank branch must be recorded for electronic disbursements.
Missing mandatory headers halt saving and highlight the exact field requiring attention.
Transaction currency conversion rates must be positive numbers matching active corporate exchange rates.
Accurate recording of bank reference details ensures smooth bank reconciliation and audit compliance.
Mandatory bank fields ensure funds transfers reach designated supplier bank accounts without return.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.

cards.title: Double-entry balance equality and tax deduction at source rules
cards.body:
Payment vouchers enforce strict mathematical equality under double-entry accounting principles.
The total debit amount across all rows must exactly equal the total credit amount.
If debits and credits do not balance, the system halts saving with an equality refusal.
Debit amounts cannot be left empty or zero on any individual recipient account line.
Credit amounts cannot be left empty or zero on any individual bank or cash payment line.
When tax deduction at source rules apply, appropriate tax deduction rules must be selected.
Proceeding without required tax deduction rules triggers confirmation warnings on screen.
Inter-book vouchers require balanced combinations of intermediate clearing accounts.
Line item currency conversions must match the active corporate exchange rate for foreign payments.
These balancing rules ensure that company ledgers remain perfectly in equilibrium at all times.
Tax deduction amounts are segregated into statutory payable accounts for government remittance.
Accurate double-entry balancing prevents discrepancies between cash books and the balance sheet.
Balancing checks prevent unbalanced journal vouchers from posting into general ledger books.

cards.title: User authorization limits, record locking, and payment cancellation
cards.body:
Payment vouchers advance through three formal operational statuses: Initial, Release, and Authorized.
Saving in Release status records the user identity and queues the voucher for signing by treasury.
User authorization limits configured in system settings restrict maximum disbursement amounts.
If the voucher amount exceeds the logged-in user limit, authorization is blocked by system checks.
Vouchers flagged as rejected by management cannot be authorized under any operational circumstances.
Once authorized, the payment voucher is completely locked against editing, modification, or deletion.
Authorizing the voucher posts credit entries to bank ledgers and debits to vendor accounts.
Reversing an authorized payment requires an official cancellation voucher entry in the accounts.
Historical audit logs capture all voucher authorizations, print events, and cheque numbers.
Locked voucher records protect corporate banking transactions from retroactive tampering.
Authorizing the voucher updates cash flow forecasts and closes matched purchase bill schedules.
This authorization control guarantees that treasury disbursements adhere to executive financial mandates.
Treasury managers verify bank account liquidity before releasing high-value payment vouchers.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.
